blanks.note: Central Bank of Iraq, Financial Statements 31 December 2025 (cbi.iq/static/uploads/up/file-178383920232205.pdf, 3.2 MB, full English statements) downloaded and the whole text grepped for external/manager/mandate/RAMP/World Bank/IBRD/Crown Agents/BlackRock/Amundi/PIMCO/UBS/Wellington/State Street/Nomura/Franklin/custodian/JPMorgan/Goldman, including the accounting-policy notes, not only the reserves note. The words 'external manager', 'externally managed' and 'fund manager' do not occur. The only outside names are in two tables that the brief excludes: the credit-rating table of 'Financial assets at amortized cost' (p. 43), which lists Asian Development Bank, AIIB, BIS, Bank of England, CADES, EBRD, EIB, IBRD (World Bank), Islamic Development Bank, JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A., KfW, MUFG, Norges Bank, People's Bank of China and the US Treasury with Fitch/Moody's/S&P columns; and the concentration-risk table (p. 44) listing the same institutions plus Standard Chartered, Citibank, QNB, National Bank of Kuwait, Euroclear, First Abu Dhabi Bank, DBS and Mizuho as counterparties by IQD exposure. Those are issuers and counterparties with rating columns, not mandates. The note on financial assets at amortised cost says only that they 'comprise debt securities and fixed-term instruments held by the Bank to fulfill its statutory mandates'. The 31 December 2024 statements (file-174851886981175.pdf) were downloaded and grepped the same way: the only hits are 'JPMorgan Chase Bank National Association' at two counterparty-table lines and 'external valuers' in the property revaluation policy.

Bank Negara Malaysia Annual Report 2023, complete book including the audited financial statements (ar2023_en_book.pdf, 59 MB, 14,539 lines of extracted text; mirror copy at repositori.mypolycc.edu.my/bitstream/123456789/2544/1/ar2023_en_book.pdf). The whole document was grepped for 'external fund manag', 'external manag', 'externally manag', 'mandates award', 'appointed as manager', RAMP, Crown Agents, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura, Franklin Templeton, World Bank and IBRD: zero hits for any manager term. The financial-statements section (Notes to the Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2023) was then isolated and grepped on the looser stems extern/manag/custod/agent: the only hits are Note 23 'Financial Risk Management', which says the Reserve Management Committee 'oversees the assessment, measurement and the control of the investment risks in the management of reserves' and controls deviation from benchmark through risk-management limits, and the related-party note on BNM acting as 'financial adviser, banker and financial agent of the Government'. No outside manager, custodian or agent is named anywhere in the report. The eleven World Bank hits are all research and technical-cooperation items (a COP28 announcement, a green-growth study, agribusiness work with ADFIM), none about reserves.

Bangladesh Bank Annual Report 2022-2023 (bb.org.bd/pub/annual/anreport/ar2022-2023.pdf, 7.7 MB, 34,000+ lines) downloaded and grepped in full: 'external fund manag', 'external manag', 'fund manager', RAMP, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura and Franklin all return zero hits, and the six World Bank hits are commodity-price citations, an IFC co-financed project and a BB-World Bank technical programme, none about reserves. The 'Reserve Management Strategy' passage, paras 12.23-12.24 of Chapter 12 'External Sector Developments' (pp. 141-142), describes the arrangement positively as in-house: reserve operations 'are carried out following the Reserve Management Guidelines (RMG) approved by the Board of Directors of BB', reserves are 'divided into two tranches viz: liquidity tranche and investment tranche', investment duration and currency benchmarks are 'set out in the RMG', and 'reserve management and investment functions have been segregated among three independent reporting units viz., Front Office, Middle Office and Back Office'. Holdings are current accounts with major central banks, T-bills, repos (including the New York Fed repo process), short-term deposits with 'reputed overseas commercial banks', gold and 'high-rated sovereign, supranational, and corporate bonds'. No outside manager is named and none is said to exist. ALSO TRIED: the FY2024-2025 report (ar2024-2025.pdf, 18 MB) was downloaded but its PDF fonts carry no ToUnicode map, so pdftotext returns 675 KB of mojibake and zero occurrences even of the string 'extern'; it is not readable without OCR of the whole 18 MB file, which was outside this round's budget. The FY2022-23 report extracts cleanly and was used instead.

CONFIRMED BUT UNNAMED, and newly documented this round. Bank of Thailand, 'Financial Statements 2025' (the separate audited statements, bot.or.th/content/dam/bot/documents/en/research-and-publications/reports/financial-reports/annual-report/Statement_2025_EN.pdf), downloaded and grepped in full. Two places state that external managers run part of the reserves, and the decisive one is in the accounting-policy note rather than the reserves note, exactly as the brief warned: Note 3.8 'Investments in securities' (p. 15) reads 'Foreign securities, including those managed by external fund managers, are held for international reserve management purposes and are measured at fair value'; and Note 24 'Other expenses' carries a line item 'External fund manager management fees' of THB 1,107 million for 2025 (THB 786 million for 2024), listed separately from 'Investment management fees' of THB 831 million (2024: THB 1,048 million). No firm is named anywhere in the document; the only other hits on 'extern' are external experts on the Audit Committee, external cloud computing services and external stakeholders. Note 29.1(2) 'Financial risk management for international reserves' gives priorities (safety, liquidity, return, risk management) and names nobody. The BOT 'Reserve Management' web page (bot.or.th/en/our-roles/financial-markets/Reserve_Management.html) was also read and names no manager; its only outside references are eligible issuer classes in the legal section. So Thailand now joins IND, SAU and QAT as a bank that confirms external managers on the record and names none — worth recording as a confirmed-unnamed case, but not filed as a tie because there is no counterparty to key it to. NEXT: BOT Annual Report 2025 narrative volume (AnnualReport_2025Eng.pdf) and any BOT procurement/appointment announcement for fund-management mandates; the fee line proves a contract exists, so a Thai public-procurement award notice is the most likely route to a name.

CONFIRMED BUT UNNAMED. BSP Annual Report 2025 (bsp.gov.ph/Media_And_Research/Annual%20Report/AnnRep_2025.pdf, 27 MB, 18,829 lines) downloaded and grepped in full. The section 'International reserves management' (p. 27) states 'The BSP also engaged the services of external fund managers. Their performance exceeded benchmarks, driven by effective interest rate strategies, timely duration positioning, and selective exposures across global and regional bond markets', and on the previous page records that 'Enhanced internal capabilities and technology also allowed the BSP to manage some outsourced portfolios in-house, reducing costs and increasing control over reserve deployment' — i.e. outsourced portfolios existed and some were brought back in. No firm is named: grepping the whole report for BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura, Franklin, Crown Agents, RAMP and IBRD returns nothing, the BIS hits are a cited Annual Economic Report, an ISO 20022 committee, Project Mandala and co-organised events, and the World Bank hits are Global Economic Prospects citations. So the Philippines is a confirmed-unnamed case. NEXT: the BSP Annual Report Volume I financial statements proper (the audited statements and notes are issued separately from this narrative volume — try the BSP 'Annual Report' list page bsp.gov.ph/Pages/MediaAndResearch/PublicationsAndReports/AnnualReport.aspx), and Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) award notices for BSP external fund management services, which is the likeliest route to a name.

Qatar Central Bank Annual Report 2020 (QCB-ANNUAL-REPORT-2020-revised-final-Sep-28.pdf, 2.4 MB, 11,269 lines; copy served by portal.usqbc.org) downloaded and grepped in full for extern, 'fund manag', 'portfolio manag', RAMP, World Bank, IBRD, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura, Franklin and custodian. No manager term occurs at all. The nine 'extern' hits are external demand, external factors and external parties in the AML discussion; the one World Bank hit is a 'World Bank Technical Team for internal consumption'. No outside manager is named and the report does not say external managers are used. This closes the 2020 annual report route only: QCB's more recent annual reports were not reached this round, and the pre-existing confirmed-but-unnamed statement recorded elsewhere on this map ('the top ten globally') is not re-found or contradicted here. NEXT: QCB Annual Report 2024 or 2025 and the separate QCB audited financial statements, from qcb.gov.qa; a named firm, not another unnamed confirmation, is what would count.

Central Bank of Kuwait, 'Annual Report 2011/2012' (cbk.gov.kw/en/images/annual-reports-2011-2012-10204_v20_tcm10-10204.pdf, 200 KB, 1,945 lines, includes the audited financial statements) downloaded and grepped in full on extern, manager/managers/managed, RAMP, Crown Agents, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura and Franklin. The only 'managed' hits are the statement headings 'Accounts Managed by the CBK on Behalf of the Government of the State of Kuwait' — the CBK managing for others, the reverse of this row — plus external borrowings and internal/external CBK mail in an IT-project list. No outside manager is named. ALSO TRIED: the combined press-economic-and-annual-report 2018/19 PDF (press-economic-report-and-annual-report-18-19-143907_v10_tcm10-143907.pdf, 388 KB) downloaded but extracts only 158 lines of text, i.e. it is substantially an image scan and would need OCR. NEXT: the CBK 53rd Annual Report for FY2024/2025, announced at cbk.gov.kw press release 202510130945, and the 51st (FY2022/2023) report; and OCR of the 2018/19 file. Note for the next round that the Kuwait Investment Authority, which does use many outside managers, is a separate sovereign fund and not this row.

The document was never read, because the host defeated both tools. The two RBI 'Half Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves' PDFs returned by search (website.rbi.org.in/documents/87730/30842423/HYRMFER7e93d0418db64573937dcfac838d0837.pdf and .../HYR041120222fefa5a5260d4723be7334cac004c3b2.pdf) both serve curl a 152 KB HTML page instead of the PDF, and WebFetch on the first is 302-redirected to https://www.rbi.org.in/ — the file itself is not served to automation by either route. Per the task instruction, the governor's on-record statement that a very small part of the reserves is run by an external manager, with no firm named, is already recorded as a confirmed-unnamed case and re-finding it would be a blank, so nothing is filed. NEXT: the same Half Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves, reached through the rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/ mirror path or the RBI Annual Report chapter 'Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves', fetched in a browser-capable tool rather than curl or WebFetch; the test remains whether any year names a firm.

The document was located but could not be downloaded. The Central Bank of Oman annual report page (cbo.gov.om/Pages/AnnualReport.aspx) gives direct PDF links for 2023, 2024 and 2025 on the host publishing.bnet.om, and curl on the 2025 file (publishing.bnet.om/sites/assets/Documents/English/Publications/AnnualReports/Annual%20Report%202025%20ENG.pdf) failed with the agent proxy reporting connect_unreachable for publishing.bnet.om:443 — the host is allowed but the egress proxy could not connect to it. cbo.gov.om itself also returned HTTP 000 to curl on a directory page, so only the WebFetch route worked on this site. NEXT: the same three PDFs (Annual Report 2025 / 2024 / 2023 ENG) fetched through WebFetch rather than curl, grepped for 'external fund manager' and the firm list; CBO publishes full English audited statements, so this remains the best untested Gulf candidate on the slice.

SAMA's own annual report was never opened this round; the budget went on the countries whose statements download cleanly. One search was spent on the trade-press route and it confirms the existing position rather than breaking it: the items returned are a Bloomberg-derived story headlined 'Saudi Central Bank Said to Pull Money From at Least Two Managers' and secondary rewrites of it (webpronews, whalesbook), none of which names a manager, and the only named mandate in the results — 'BlackRock wins $5bn Saudi SWF mandate' (alternativeswatch.com, April 2024) and a BlackRock Saudi infrastructure-fund mandate (salaamgateway) — are the Public Investment Fund, a sovereign wealth fund and not the central bank, so neither can be filed here. The map's existing confirmed-but-unnamed SAMA statement is untouched. NEXT: SAMA Annual Report and the separate SAMA audited financial statements from sama.gov.sa, grepped for 'external' and the firm list; and, since the trade-press route has now failed twice, treat a named firm in SAMA's own statements as the only acceptable source.

Never opened — no document for Russia was fetched this round. NEXT, unchanged from round 68: the Bank of Russia Annual Report section on the management of foreign currency and gold assets (cbr.ru, English edition), plus the separate quarterly/annual review of foreign exchange and gold asset management that the CBR publishes. checked_not_in_assignment: No country outside the twelve assigned codes was pursued or filed. One near-miss worth stating: the Central Bank of Iraq's 2025 statements list People's Bank of China, Norges Bank, Bank of England and the BIS among its issuers and counterparties, which could be misread as ties for CHN, NOR, GBR or a BIS record. They are issuer and counterparty rating tables, which the brief excludes, and all of them sit in the Iraq record anyway, so nothing was filed for any of them.

The Kuwait Investment Authority and the Saudi Public Investment Fund both came up while working KWT and SAU. Both are sovereign wealth funds, not central banks, so they are outside this map's unit of record entirely; no record and no country was added for them.
